title: Classification / Odd One Out — In-Depth Guide — Part 9 of 16

questions.question: What does 'Palindrome Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of words/numbers all read the same forwards and backwards, with one breaking that pattern
Whether words share a common length only
questions.rationale: This tests whether items are palindromes (reading the same forwards and backwards), identifying the one that isn't.

questions.question: What does 'Repeated Digit Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of numbers all contain a repeated digit, with one number having no repeated digits
Whether numbers share a digit sum
questions.rationale: This tests whether numbers share the property of containing a repeated digit, identifying the exception with all-unique digits.

questions.question: What does 'Same-Digit Sum Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of numbers all share the identical digit sum, with one number having a different digit sum
Whether numbers are all perfect squares
questions.rationale: This tests whether all numbers in a group share the exact same digit sum, identifying the one with a differing digit sum.

questions.question: What does 'Letter Pair Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of letter pairs share a consistent relationship (like a fixed shift), with one pair breaking it
questions.rationale: This tests whether a set of letter pairs share a consistent relationship, such as a fixed alphabet shift, identifying the pair that doesn't follow it.

questions.question: What does 'Word Pattern Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of words share a common structural pattern (like a repeated syllable structure), with one breaking it
questions.rationale: This tests whether words share a common structural pattern, identifying the word that breaks that shared structural rule.

questions.question: What does 'Common Prefix' classification test?
options: Whether a group of words all share the same starting letters (prefix), with one word having a different prefix
questions.rationale: This tests whether words share a common prefix (starting letters), identifying the word that starts differently.

questions.question: What does 'Common Suffix' classification test, in contrast?
options: Whether a group of words all share the same ending letters (suffix), with one word having a different suffix
questions.rationale: This tests whether words share a common suffix (ending letters), identifying the word that ends differently.

questions.question: What is the key distinction 'Meaning vs Spelling' highlights in classification?
options: That meaning and spelling are always identical properties
That a group might be connected by meaning-based similarity or by spelling-based similarity, and these are different bases for classification
That spelling never matters in classification
That meaning never matters in classification
questions.rationale: This distinguishes classification based on shared meaning from classification based on shared spelling patterns — two genuinely different bases that shouldn't be conflated.

questions.question: What is the 'Homophone Trap'?
options: Mistaking words that sound alike (homophones) for words that are actually spelled or related the same way
A trap that only applies to numbers
A trap with no practical relevance
questions.rationale: The homophone trap involves mistaking words that merely sound alike for words that share a genuine spelling or meaning-based relationship, when they're actually unrelated in the relevant sense.

questions.question: What does 'General Knowledge Classification' broadly draw on?
options: Real-world factual knowledge across domains (science, geography, etc.) to determine shared categories
questions.rationale: This type of classification draws on broader factual, real-world knowledge across various domains to determine what category connects a group of items.
